content.title: ‘Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen’ Loses Steam: Review
content.text: Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen Could’ve Been a Classic By , a Vulture TV critic who also covers film and pop culture. She is a juror for the Peabody Awards. Light spoilers follow for Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen, which premiered with all eight episodes on Netflix on March 26. A woman with no family, a mysterious background, and a nearly clairvoyant sense of when things around her are turning cosmically wrong gets engaged to a rich, pedigreed, happy-go-lucky guy. There are deadly miscommunications among relatives, an injured animal that becomes a reflection of the wounded protagonist, and buckets of viscera. This is the kind of conflict setup any horror fan would recognize, but Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen rearranges it all in such a deft, inspired way that if this project were shorter and tighter, it would be a classic of the genre. Created by Haley Z. Boston, who worked on the Netflix horror series Brand New Cherry Flavor and Guillermo del Toro’s Cabinet of Curiosities, and produced by the Duffer Brothers, Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen follows Rachel (Camila Morrone) and Nicky (Adam DiMarco) in the days leading up to their wedding. They met in an airport three years ago when Rachel refused to board her flight because of a bad feeling and Nicky believed her warning. Instead, they drove together from Austin to Chicago and fell in love along the way. Morrone plays Rachel as a woman who can’t quite believe her luck and keeps touching her partner to check that he’s real. Here’s this guy who gets her, who accepts her for whatever sixth sense she may possess, and she’s so charmed by that love — so overwhelmed by it — that she accepts his proposal despite her previous hesitations about marriage.
